newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso calm about economy, trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso calm about economy, trade.

text.p: Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said he was completely calm about the economy, the trade deficit and the red ink in the public sector accounts.
"Everything is under control," he told reporters.
Cardoso predicted that the operational public sector deficit for 1996 would be about 2.5 percent of gross domestic product.

This is in contrast to Finance Minister Pedro Malan and other members of the government's economics team, who have conceded that 1996 will likely end with an opperational deficit of about 3.5 percent of GDP, falling to 2.5 percent next year.
But Cardoso said the result could be lower because "we are making adjustments in the states".
The president urged calm over Brazil's widening trade deficit, which has startled markets.
"We must stop this obsession with looking at the deficit day by day, seeing how much Brazil exports every day. We will only know what the outcome is at the end of the year," he said.
Cardoso added the country should stop thinking as if the economy were heading into "insurmountable" problems.
"They are surmountable. And we will overcome them," he said. "I am completely calm about the economic situation."

Cardoso said he was not worried about rattled markets, saying it was a trader's job to be nervous one day and calm the next. "For those who act in the name of the country, it is not like that," he said.
The president reiterated a vow not to be pressured by debt-ridden states into generous refinancing agreements.
"We will only negotiate with those who are carrying out adjustments. It's not worth throwing money at those who aren't because this isn't my money, it's the people's," he said.
